data.title: Record a reusable 3D production receipt
data.summary: One completed local candidate export and its measured file/dimension data. An LLM-assisted recipe with a concrete practice case, visual procedure and review gates.

facts.text: The Python API can inspect and modify Blender data and run tools.

prerequisites: An authorized Claude Code / Codex / existing Studio environment and a recorded tool version. Blender-specific references here are pinned to the 4.5 manual; check differences in your installed version.
Practice inputs: One completed local candidate export and its measured file/dimension data.

Permission to use the source assets and a writable derived-output location. Use a disposable project copy for edits. An MCP connection is optional; reviewed scripts or manual tool actions can follow the same procedure.
steps: Inspect the existing project, asset registry and target runtime for an equivalent production receipt workflow. Reuse the closest source and preserve its original files.

Give Claude Code, Codex or another authorized coding assistant this practice brief: One completed local candidate export and its measured file/dimension data. Ask for a small plan and parameter/script diff; verify names and APIs against the installed tool version before applying it.
Reuse the existing batch receipt format and collect source revision, parameters and output hash
Record only actually measured timings, geometry counts and validation results
Link the receipt to the candidate and leave absent measurements explicitly unknown

Save the derived candidate separately, record software versions and source/output identities, then perform the acceptance checks. Keep unresolved quality, performance and rights questions in the receipt.
data.output: A versioned record a reusable 3d production receipt candidate, the input/parameter table, source identity and a review receipt with the checks below.
validation: Every reported metric has a measurement method and scope
The receipt names unresolved visual, rights and device gates
Record actual observations separately from expected results; missing tests remain unrun.
limitations: A receipt is agent-authored evidence until independently checked and does not approve production.
Sintra-authored proposal, not an executed Blender/engine/solver test. The diagram illustrates the procedure and is not a render or execution receipt.
Cloud chat cannot directly control a local 3D app without an appropriate authorized bridge. Tool access, model availability, paid services and rendering resources must be checked separately.
tips: Use asset triangles and full-scene rendered triangles as different metrics.
Let the LLM draft and explain bounded changes; use deterministic software to measure geometry, calculate trajectories and validate files.

data.prompt: Help me record a reusable 3d production receipt in [existing authorized project]. First find an equivalent asset/workflow and inspect the installed tool version. Practice brief: One completed local candidate export and its measured file/dimension data. Propose the smallest parameter or script diff and explain each tool action. Follow the linked procedure, preserve original assets and stop on missing inputs or unsupported APIs. Check: Every reported metric has a measurement method and scope; The receipt names unresolved visual, rights and device gates. Return actual observations, source/output identities and blockers. Do not call expected results completed tests or publish private source paths.

troubleshooting.symptom: An operator, node socket or exporter option is unavailable
troubleshooting.action: Stop and inspect the installed tool/version documentation; adapt the smallest affected step rather than guessing an API name.

troubleshooting.symptom: The candidate fails its stated review condition
troubleshooting.action: Return to the last accepted source/parameter set, reduce to one representative case and record the failed observation. Use asset triangles and full-scene rendered triangles as different metrics.
